prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes: Normal Operations(typical service durations unless Handling Resource Planner constraint/stand stalls), Adverse Weather(bus/loader/tow padded), Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved shorter cycles; no release-on-ready pushback surges), Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell: proposes TOBT from airside capacity+ground path; TOBT conditional if resources late; locks at freeze horizon unless exception/override recorded; separates ATC vs handling delay; records airspace alerts, acks, decisions in Audit Event Ledger. Parts: Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone(flags imbalancing TOBTs); Capacity Assessment Module(Airport Capacity Plan, Acceptance Rate; late reduction→recalculates Airport Acceptance Rate→planning cycle; restriction=time-bounded throughput cut); Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor(CTT; priority emergency/national>scheduled>GA; delays logged; revises only within operating-state authority+fairness rules); Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove(value, confidence, reason code; readiness changes to authenticated users; feasibility→Saffron, Aircraft Operator Representative; restriction status, effect, coordination notes→Common Situation Display); Departure Metering Service(aligns TOBT/CTT; current capacity adjusts release guidance, preserves coordinated CTT where feasible; CTT→Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf, must refresh sequence advisories when restriction changes routes/spacing; Business Rules Registry spacing); North/South Runway Meter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensor; Ramp Movement Board=Skylark; Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard(→CAM); Flight Data Exchange(intent→DMS); Airline Interface Adapter; Time Synchronization Service; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Collaborative Decision Log; Identity Access Service(role-gated); Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern(domain routing; airspace alerts→flow mgmt, sector planning, tower, operator roles; subscription rules from Business Rules Registry; elevated severity in Adverse Weather/Capacity Reduction when compounding constraints); Digital Briefing Room; Sector Load Monitor(demand vs reduced sector capacity, overload intervals); Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner(hard constraint; tow, buses, loaders, stairs, GPU, air start, water; Stand Tow Request Form); Arrival Regulation Console(applies reductions to inbound flows at feeder sectors/metering fixes);

Document units:
S345: The Digital Briefing Room provides a common venue for the Regional Flow Manager, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor, and Airport Duty Manager to confirm the active interpretation of the restriction.
S346: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares planned capacity, issued alerts, operator acknowledgements, and realized delay to determine whether the restriction handling process supported timely and consistent decisions.
S347: Departure metering extends the restriction handling process by deciding where delay is best absorbed before aircraft begin taxi.
S348: The Departure Metering Service, known operationally as Emberline, is the system function that converts runway demand into controlled stand delay before aircraft enter the taxi stream.
S349: The metering process starts when the Regional Flow Platform normalizes each Flight Intent Message against the current Airport Capacity Plan.
S350: The Demand Prediction Service estimates the departure demand profile by stand, apron area, runway, and departure fix.
S351: The Capacity Assessment Module compares that demand with the active Airport Acceptance Rate, runway configuration, taxiway constraints, and sector limits.
S352: The Departure Metering Service then derives a feasible Target Off Block Time that protects the Calculated Takeoff Time without overloading the surface movement area.
S353: Stand absorption is preferred when the aircraft can remain connected to normal operator processes and when holding at the gate will not create a gate conflict.
S354: Pushback windows are coordinated as narrow time bands that give the flight crew, ramp team, and tower sequence a common expectation without treating the window as a clearance to move.
S355: Blueharbor shall adjust allocated departure times when metering rules require additional stand absorption to preserve the planned runway sequence.
S356: Halcyon records the agreed pushback window rationale in the coordination notes before the plan is released to operational users.
S357: The Ramp Control Lead reviews the proposed windows against apron congestion, towing activity, and aircraft readiness before accepting them for local execution.
S358: The Tower Supervisor monitors whether the planned release rate remains compatible with departure spacing and runway crossing demand.
S359: The North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter maintain independent queue counts so that one runway cannot mask an excess queue on the other runway.
S360: Surface surveillance inputs from the Surface Surveillance Adapter are used to confirm the actual number of aircraft waiting at runway holding points.
S361: The Ramp Movement Board produces the Fuel Truck Hold Advice when metering decisions require servicing activity to remain clear of an aircraft that is being held at stand.
